suggestions.rationale: Depression is a substantial and clinically recognized comorbidity in Parkinson disease, but prevalence evidence does not establish that Parkinson disease caused an individual's depressive disorder. A systematic review/meta-analysis of depression-detection studies in adult outpatients with Parkinson disease found a pooled major-depression prevalence of 22.9%. This mapping therefore supports association/comorbidity research only; individual chronology, prodromal mood symptoms, disability burden, medications, sleep, pain, cognition, psychosocial factors, and other psychiatric causes must be reviewed before any secondary theory is advanced.
evidenceGaps: Clinical diagnosis and chronology of Parkinson disease and depressive disorder
Whether depressive symptoms predated motor Parkinson disease or emerged later in the disease course
Medication, sleep, pain, cognitive, functional, and psychosocial contributors to depression
Assessment for other psychiatric or neurological explanations
Qualified clinician assessment distinguishing common comorbidity from individual causation or aggravation

sourceReferences.citation: Goodarzi Z, Mrklas KJ, Roberts DJ, et al. Detecting depression in Parkinson disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis. Neurology. 2016;87(4):426-437. PMID 27358339
sourceReferences.note: Systematic review/meta-analysis of 21 studies found pooled major-depression prevalence of 22.9% in adult outpatients with Parkinson disease and evaluated validated depression-detection tools. Supports association/comorbidity research, not an individual causal direction.
